subject: Order of boxes in faceted boxplots

messages.author: 3afed3696e5ae3c2
messages.subject: Order of boxes in faceted boxplots
parts:
Dear ggplot2 users,

I am new to this group and I would first like to thank Hadley for this
wonderful package!

My question is related to faceted boxplots and I have attached sample
code to illustrate the problem I have:

Example 1)
## Ordering works fine
tier1 <- letters[1:10]
tier2 <- c(rep("tier-a",5), rep("tier-b",5))
values <- runif(10, 1, 10)
d <- data.frame(tier1, tier2, values)
gg <- ggplot(d)
gg + geom_bar(aes(x=reorder(tier1, values), y=values)) + facet_wrap
(~tier2, scales="free")

Example 2)
## Ordering does not work
tier1 <- c("d", "b", "e", "a", "f", "f", "a", "b", "g", "e")
tier2 <- c(rep("tier-a",5), rep("tier-b",5))
values <- runif(10, 1, 10)
d <- data.frame(tier1, tier2, values)
gg <- ggplot(d)
gg + geom_bar(aes(x=reorder(tier1, values), y=values)) + facet_wrap
(~tier2, scales="free")

In example one the ordering of boxes in the boxplot works absolutely
perfect. However, in the second example the ordering does not work. I
assume it has something to do with repeating values in vector "tier1".
Does anyone know how to circumvent this problem. I am not sure whether
this might be a bug in ggplot.

Many thanks for your help!

Best,

David

I don't think this is something ggplot can do. See, for example:

http://learnr.wordpress.com/2009/07/02/ggplot2-version-of-figures-in-lattice-multivariate-data-visualization-with-r-part-4/#_figure_4_7

In particular, look at

(~tier2)

using your second example. Here, the empty levels of the factor are
not suppressed, and you see the facets have the x-axis categories in
the same order. In fact, it is the same order as the levels in

with(d, reorder(tier1, values))

which suggests that the ordering takes place before the data is split
for faceting. Also note that by default reorder sorts by the average
of all the values in the level.

--Brian Diggs

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Order of boxes in faceted boxplots
parts:
> using your second example.  Here, the empty levels of the factor are
> not suppressed, and you see the facets have the x-axis categories in
> the same order.  In fact, it is the same order as the levels in
>
> with(d, reorder(tier1, values))

The order levels on categorical axis is defined by the order of the
underlying levels. A factor has a single ordering, so you're right
that this can't be accomplished in ggplot2 with facetting. Work
arounds:

* two separate plots
* reorder(paste(tier1, teir2), values)

Hadley
